styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical blue sign board with white Korean text (편의) on a dark navy frame. It has about 3 shading steps: a mid blue face, a lighter edge or highlight, and a dark navy outline. The measured facts are reasonable: 9 visible tones per tile (bus-shelter 6, kiosk 12, vending 20), 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted navy and not black. Against the richer references it still looks thinner. Kiosk-a and vending-a show striped awnings, panels, highlights and multi-step shading, while the sign is mostly a flat blue slab with text and no visible grain, speckle or edge highlights. Its density falls between bus-shelter and kiosk. It is a simple sign and not the richest piece, but it sits at or above the weakest reference (bus-shelter) and does not read as a flat sticker. When in doubt this should fail, but the numbers and tinted outline support a pass only if the artist accepts a simple sign. On balance the shading depth is shallower than the kiosk and vending references.
